employee_master.title: HR 1 — The Employee Master & Organisational Structure
employee_master.desc: The foundation of the people certification: the employee as the fifth master, the person's record and its custody frame, the organisational trees and the reporting spine, employment types and the status discipline, the user link and self-service, master governance, and the joins to every other track.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — The people layer: the fifth master
lessons.html:
Welcome to the fifth certification. Four tracks taught four masters — the customer, the supplier, the item, the account — and every one of them was operated BY people this academy kept naming without recording: the storekeeper whose custody Inventory 1 framed, the till operator whose sessions Accounts 3 reconciled, the approver whose two names every threshold demanded. This track records them: the people layer — the employee as the fifth master, and the machinery that manages a workforce from its first application to its last working day.

What HR-in-the-system buys. The same purchase every master made, at its most personal: ONE RECORD per person (the employee master — this module), holding the whole lifecycle (hired, confirmed, promoted, transferred, developed, separated — modules 2-7 in order), operated by DOCUMENTS (the leave application, the appraisal, the transfer letter — each an auditable event, not a corridor conversation), read by RHYTHMS (the attendance reads, the leave planning, the appraisal cycles), and structured to survive its administrators (module 8's handover, because the HR-in-one-head disease is the founder-bottleneck's most personal organ). The firm whose people machinery runs on the system answers every people question — who works here, since when, on what terms, approved by whom, developed how — from one place; the firm whose HR lives in a folder and a memory answers none of them without archaeology, and pays for it precisely at the worst moments: the dispute, the audit, the departure.

The scope line, drawn deliberately. This track EXCLUDES payroll — not because payroll is unimportant but because it is a different discipline with a different owner: the salary computation, the statutory custodies, the payment run belong to the finance function (the Accounts track's modules 2 and 5 already carry the payroll journal and the PAYE machinery), and the boundary between the two is itself curriculum: HR OWNS the inputs payroll consumes — who is employed (this module), who attended (module 3), who was on leave (module 4), who was promoted to what grade (module 7) — and the clean handoff of those inputs, on a calendar, is where the two functions mesh. A firm whose HR and payroll disagree about who worked in March has a boundary problem this track's disciplines prevent.

The tone this track carries. One difference from every prior track, named at the door: the other masters were RECORDS OF THINGS — items, accounts, companies. This master is a record OF A PERSON, and that changes the governance's flavour throughout: the data is held in CUSTODY (confidentiality as a design requirement, not a courtesy — module 8 gives it structure), the documents affect livelihoods (the warning letter, the appraisal rating, the separation — each carrying procedural fairness as a discipline, module 7's core), and the system's job is to make the firm's dealings with its people CONSISTENT and EVIDENCED — which protects the honest employee exactly as the counting disciplines protected the honest custodian: the academy's oldest framing, now applied to the people it was always quietly about.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The employee master: anatomy of the person's record
lessons.html:
The record itself, section by section — because every module ahead reads or writes some part of it, and the consultant must know exactly what lives where.

  • Identity — the person's names (as their legal documents state them — the record that will feed contracts, statutory filings, and certificates does not improvise spellings), the employee NUMBER (the naming-series law's fifth appearance: chosen once, never re-used — a departed employee's number is retired with them, because re-issued numbers merge two people's histories in every report forever), photograph, date of birth, gender, marital status.
  • Employment — the fields the whole system reads: date of joining (the anchor of tenure, probation, leave accrual, and every service computation), employment TYPE (Chapter 4), STATUS (Active, on notice, Left — Chapter 4's discipline), the org placement (company, branch, department, designation, grade — Chapter 3), and reports to — the manager field, which Chapter 3 will crown as the approval spine.
  • Contacts & emergency — personal and company contact details, address, and the emergency contact whose absence is only ever discovered on the day it is needed: the field the annual verification (Chapter 6) checks first, because it is the one the firm hopes never to use and must never find stale.
  • Identifiers & compliance — the national and tax identifiers the Nigerian employment context requires (the tax identification the PAYE machinery will reference — held here, consumed by the payroll function across the boundary), bank details for that same handoff, and pension administrator details (the employee's chosen PFA — Accounts 5 met the remittance side; the CHOICE lives here).
  • Documents — the attachment discipline: the offer and contract, the credentials as verified (Chapter's 6 verification note), the ID copies, and later the lifecycle's paper trail (confirmations, promotion letters, warnings — modules 2 and 7 file into this record). The employee master is the FILE — the paper folder's successor, complete or the folder quietly remains the real record (Chapter 9's pattern).
  • Dates that govern — beyond joining: confirmation date (probation's end — module 2), contract end dates for fixed-term staff (Chapter 4 — an expiry the system must see coming), and the document-expiry family Chapter 6 tracks.

The custody frame, operationalised. This record holds a person's identity documents, bank details, family contacts, and — as the lifecycle accumulates — their disciplinary and performance history: data whose exposure harms a real person, held under a data-protection duty Nigerian law now articulates (the consultant's altitude: a registered duty of care over personal data exists, its details are the compliance professional's terrain, and the SYSTEM'S contribution is structural — the permission design of Chapter 5 and module 8 that makes who can see what a configuration, not a hope). The working rule taught from day one: employee data is read on NEED, not curiosity — and the system's role-based fences are how the rule survives staff turnover in HR itself.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The organisational structure: trees, lists & the spine
lessons.html:
The employee record places its person INTO a structure, and the structure is this academy's favourite subject wearing its people clothes: trees and lists, designed from what must be read — plus one field that outranks them all.

The structural vocabulary. Company — the legal employer (the multi-company frontier of Accounts 8: people are employed by legal persons, and the employee of the trading company is not the employee of the property company); branch — the location (the field that will align with the warehouse tree and cost centers — Chapter 7's join); department — the functional grouping (Operations, Sales, Finance, Admin — the tree that mirrors how work is actually organised); designation — the role's name (Storekeeper, Branch Manager, Accountant — a LIST, governed like every value list this academy has met: named owner, conventions, no duplicates-by-spelling); and grade — the level (the band structure that will carry benefit entitlements and leave policies — module 4 reads it — and, across the boundary, the payroll structure's key).

Designing the structure: the accountability law, again. The design hour runs on the cost-center chapter's exact logic (Accounts 6), because it is the same design: departments mirror ACCOUNTABILITY (a department exists when someone owns it and its people are managed as a group — the eleven-person firm needs three or four, not nine), the tree stays SHALLOW (the two-level rule, fifth appearance), designations name real roles (the vanity org chart — Senior Executive Assistant Coordinator titles for an eleven-person firm — is chart sprawl's people edition, and it costs real money later when grades and policies attach to inflated titles), and the whole structure aligns with the cost-center tree it shadows (the department that is also a cost center reads its people and its money as one unit — the alignment Chapter 7 completes). The change discipline transfers whole: restructures are EVENTS (the department merged, the designations renamed — with the history's treatment decided deliberately), never casual edits.

The reporting spine. The reports-to field — each employee's named manager — deserves its own section because it is the structure's living part: the trees say where people SIT; the spine says who ANSWERS FOR whom, and the system runs its workflows along it — the leave application routing to the applicant's manager (module 4), the appraisal conducted by the manager (module 5), the expense claim, the shift change, the resignation notice all riding the same field. The disciplines that keep the spine honest: EVERY active employee has a manager (the spine with gaps strands workflows — the leave request that routes nowhere), the spine is a TREE (no cycles, no self-reporting; the founder at the root), it is MAINTAINED at every lifecycle event (the promotion that moves a manager without re-pointing their reports breaks every workflow beneath them — module 7's transfer discipline), and it reflects REALITY (the spine that says A reports to B while everyone knows A reports to C routes every approval to the wrong desk — the org chart of record and the org chart of fact must be the same chart, which is a governance conversation before it is a data entry).

The structure's readers. Why the design matters beyond tidiness: headcount reads by department and branch (module 8's analytics), leave and attendance policies attach by grade and branch (modules 3-4), approval chains ride the spine, and the payroll boundary consumes the grades — every downstream module reads this chapter's decisions, which is the definition of a master done right, and the reason the design hour happens at implementation with the owner in the room rather than being reverse-engineered from habits later.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Employment types & the status discipline
lessons.html:
Two small fields govern more downstream behaviour than any others on the record: the employment TYPE and the STATUS. The taxonomy, and the discipline.

The types. The working set for Nigerian trading firms: full-time (the permanent core), part-time (the retail reality — the weekend till staff, the market-day extras), contract / fixed-term (employed to a date — the type whose END DATE is a first-class field the system must see coming: the contract expiring unnoticed converts a deliberate arrangement into an accidental one, with legal implications the employment lawyer owns and the expiry-tracking machinery of Chapter 6 prevents), intern / trainee (the pipeline the academy's own onboarding curriculum serves — module 6's terrain), and the casual labour reality of warehouse peaks (engaged properly or not at all — the daily-paid loader who exists in no system is a liability wearing a wheelbarrow: unrecorded, uninsured, and unprovable in every direction). The type drives policy attachment (leave entitlements differ by type — module 4), benefits eligibility, and the statutory obligations the accountant confirms per type — which is why the type is set at CREATION from the offer's terms (module 2's handoff) and changed only as the lifecycle event it is (the intern confirmed to full-time is module 7's promotion machinery, not an edit).

The statuses. The record's lifecycle state: Active (the working population — every report's default filter), the notice-period states where used (resignation submitted, exit in progress — module 7's machinery), Left (separated — the terminal state that Chapter 2's number-retirement law protects), and the probation overlay (the confirmed/unconfirmed distinction riding the confirmation-date field — module 2 runs probation as a process; this field records its outcome). The status discipline is the chapter's conviction: statuses drive EVERYTHING downstream — the Active filter defines headcount (the analytics of module 8 are only as true as the statuses), leave accrual runs for active staff (the departed employee still accruing leave is a liability quietly growing — module 4), attendance expects the active roster (module 3's absence reads misfire when ghosts remain), approval spines break when a Left manager still holds reports (Chapter 3's maintenance law), and — across the boundary — payroll pays the active list, which makes a stale status literally expensive: the ghost employee (left in fact, Active in the system) is the people layer's phantom stock, and like every phantom this academy has met, it corrupts every read that touches it until someone posts the truth.

The status change as document. The cure is the academy's standard one: statuses change by DOCUMENTED EVENTS, not edits — the separation process (module 7) sets Left with its date and its paper trail; the confirmation process sets confirmed with its letter; the contract renewal extends the end date with its addendum — each change carrying who, when, why, and the attachment. A status history that reads as a sequence of documents is an employment history that survives any dispute; one that reads as unexplained edits is the folder-and-memory system wearing a database costume — and the monthly status hygiene read (the Active list walked against reality: does everyone on it still work here? does everyone working here appear on it?) is the people layer's smallest, highest-yield ritual, module 8's calendar carrying it from this chapter forward.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — The user link: self-service & the joined identity
lessons.html:
The employee record describes a person; the USER account lets that person act — and the link between the two is where the people layer becomes participatory instead of administrative. The join, its dividends, and its governance.

The join. Each employee record links to a system user (their login), and the join creates the identity the workflows need: the person who logs in IS employee so-and-so, which means the system can show them THEIR record, route THEIR requests along THEIR spine, and stamp THEIR documents with an identity nobody typed. Not every employee needs a user (the warehouse loader whose attendance is captured at a device may never log in — the record exists regardless; the user is optional), but every user who is staff should link to their employee record — the unlinked staff user is a workflow orphan whose leave requests route nowhere and whose approvals carry no organisational weight.

Self-service: the dividend. What the join buys, itemised — and it is the people layer's biggest efficiency purchase: employees SEE their own record (their details, their leave balance, their attendance history, their documents — the transparency that kills a whole category of HR queries: the balance question answered by a glance instead of an email), REQUEST through documents (the leave application, the attendance regularisation, the expense claim — each born as a document in the right queue instead of a corridor conversation someone must remember to transcribe), UPDATE what is theirs to update (the phone number, the address, the emergency contact — with the governed fields fenced: Chapter 6 draws the line between self-service fields and HR-only fields), and RECEIVE what is theirs to receive (the payslip across the boundary, the appraisal form, the policy acknowledgment). The culture note the consultant carries: self-service adoption is a TRAINING outcome, not a toggle — the workforce that learns week one that requests go through the system (because paper requests are politely redirected, every time) builds the habit; the one where both channels stay open forever builds neither.

Approvals riding the spine. The join plus the reports-to field is the approval machinery: the leave application knows its approver (the applicant's manager, from the spine), the workflow escalates along the tree, and the approval lands stamped and dated — module 4 will run this at full depth; this chapter's contribution is the wiring insight that the SPINE is the single point of maintenance: fix the manager field and every workflow above it self-corrects, which is why Chapter 3 made its maintenance a law.

The permission frame. The join's governance, previewed for module 8's full treatment: the employee role sees SELF (own record, own requests, own balances — and nothing of anyone else's), the manager sees their TEAM (the reports beneath them — their leave calendar, their attendance, their appraisals: the spine defining the visibility exactly as it defines the routing), and HR sees the population — with the sensitive layers (disciplinary records, medical notes where held, the compensation fields across the boundary) fenced tighter still. The design conviction, stated here because the user link is where violations happen: people data leaks along over-broad permissions, not through dramatic breaches — the report every user can run, the list view with one column too many — and the permission walk (module 8) audits exactly those edges. Confidentiality is a configuration before it is a policy.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Governing the people master
lessons.html:
The fifth master gets the governance every master earned — creation gated, changes evented, expiries tracked, and the annual verification — with the custody flavour Chapter 1 promised. The governance chapter.

Creation: one door. Employee records are created by HR (or the office holding the HR hat — the sizing honesty as always) through ONE flow: the recruitment pipeline's conversion (module 2 — the applicant who accepted becomes the employee, carrying the offer's terms so the record is born from its documents), or the governed direct creation for the rare walk-in hire (with the same checklist: documents collected, credentials sighted, identifiers captured, the duplicate check run — the person who worked here before, left, and returned is a REHIRE with history, not a duplicate: the record linked or the histories merge-proofed, because two records for one person is the duplicate-jungle disease at its most personally consequential — split leave histories, split tenure, split everything).

Changes: fields have owners. The field-level governance the custody frame demands: self-service fields (contacts, address, emergency contact — the person's own, updated freely with the change logged), HR-governed fields (the org placement, type, status, grade, dates — changed only by the lifecycle documents that own them: Chapter 4's law, generalised), and the joined-function fields (bank details — the fraud-relevant field: changed by a governed process with verification, because the masters-not-messages defence of the money tracks applies to salaries exactly as it applied to supplier payments — the my account changed email the week before payday gets the same known-channel verification, and the payroll boundary is notified of every change through the standing handoff, never a side note).

Expiry tracking: the calendar in the record. The people master carries dates that EXPIRE, and the system's job is to see them coming: fixed-term contract end dates (Chapter 4's conviction — surfaced 60 and 30 days out, so renewal or separation is a decision, not an accident), probation ends (the confirmation due — module 2: the probation that lapses unaddressed converts to confirmation by default in most readings of Nigerian practice, which is fine when intended and expensive when not — the employment lawyer's terrain, the system's reminder), document expiries where the role carries them (the driver's licence for the van custodian — Inventory 6's driver accountability meeting this track; the professional licences of the pharmacist superintendent — the regulated trade's compliance riding an HR field; work permits for expatriate staff), and certification expiries (module 6's training layer feeding back — the forklift certificate, the first-aider's renewal). The expiry read is a standing worklist — dated, owned, worked — the aging-report discipline of four tracks applied to the calendar inside the person's record.

The annual verification. The people master's cycle count: annually (and at every lifecycle event as a touch-point), each employee confirms their record's accuracy — contacts current, emergency contact reachable, documents complete — through self-service where the join exists, through a signed form where it does not; HR reconciles the returned confirmations, chases the silent, and files the completion. Twenty minutes per employee per year, and the dividend lands exactly where Chapter 2 warned: the emergency contact that answers, the address that receives the letter, the record that stands up in the dispute. The master that is verified annually is a master; the one that is not is a snapshot aging toward fiction — the counting law's people edition, closing the governance loop.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — The people layer meets the other four
lessons.html:
Four tracks named people this track now records — and the joins between the employee master and the other masters are where the academy's layers become one system. The join map.

  • The custodian — Inventory 1 made every warehouse answer to a person; the employee record IS that person, and the join completes the design: the warehouse's custodian named as an employee (not a free-text name that survives their departure as a ghost), the user-permission restrictions (the branch user fenced to their leaves) riding the same identity, and the custody handover at transfer or separation (module 7) triggering the warehouse machinery's own handover — the count that confirms custody before it changes hands, now scheduled by an HR event instead of remembered by luck.
  • The till operator & the van custodian — Accounts 3's sessions and Inventory 6's tailgates both reconcile per PERSON: the operator identity on every session is the employee, their clean-close streaks and variance rates are readable per employee record — and module 5 will make the connection explicit: the operational reads four tracks built (accuracy rates, clean sessions, count records) are PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE, sitting ready for the appraisal that references records instead of impressions.
  • The salesperson — the selling track's sales-team machinery joins here: the salesperson record linked to the employee, targets and attributions riding the join, the commission computations (across the payroll boundary) fed by it.
  • The approver — every two-names pattern this academy installed (the write-off's signatures, the payment run's releaser, the journal's second eyes) is ultimately a PERSON holding a role; the employee lifecycle maintains those holdings (the approver who resigns triggers the mandate-review discipline — Accounts 3's same-week signatory removal, now fired by the HR event that knows first), which is the deepest join of all: the HR system knows about departures before every other control does, and the separation checklist (module 7) is where every other track's access gets revoked.
  • The branch & cost center alignment — the employee's branch aligns with the warehouse tree's branches and the cost-center tree's leaves (the three trees naming the same operational units — the design hour of Chapter 3 checking the alignment deliberately), so that the branch's people, stock, and money read as one unit: the branch scorecard (Inventory 6), the branch P&L (Accounts 6), and the branch headcount (module 8) describing one thing three ways — and, across the boundary, the payroll cost landing on the cost center where the person works, which is Accounts 6's addressed-payroll line closing its loop.

The join discipline. One rule governs all of them: joins are made by LINK, not by retyping (the free-text name that drifts from the record it meant is the join that silently breaks), and the separation checklist is the join map read in reverse — every link the person holds, listed and resolved before Left is final. The people layer, joined this way, is not a parallel HR system beside the business; it is the business's own structure, finally knowing who its people are.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's people layer is born
lessons.html:
The fifth master, installed. The firm this academy has grown — eleven people at the start of the Selling track, near thirty by the Accounts track's close — finally gets its people layer, and every chapter clocks in.

The load (Ch. 2, 6). The existing workforce — 27 people across three branches and head office — enters properly: records created from documents (contracts pulled from the paper folders, identifiers captured, credentials sighted and marked verified where originals were produced; the two files with missing contracts flagged and regularised with the employment adviser — the load surfacing the paper gaps exactly as the opening stock count surfaced the phantom cartons), employee numbers issued from the series (the decade view), photographs taken in an afternoon, and the duplicate check earning its keep once: a returning employee — left year one, rehired at Akure — nearly loaded fresh; caught, linked as the rehire she is, tenure history whole.

The structure designed (Ch. 3). The design hour with the MD: four departments (Operations, Sales & Service, Finance & Admin, and the Distribution unit — shallow, owned, real), designations rationalised (eleven titles collapse to eight that name actual roles — the Senior Officer II vanity retired), three grades (the band structure the leave policies of module 4 will attach to), and the three-tree alignment checked deliberately: branches, warehouses, cost centers naming the same units, one row per unit on the alignment sheet. The reporting spine wired last and checked as a tree: every active employee a manager, no gaps, no cycles, the MD at the root — and one reality correction made out loud (the spine said the Akure supervisor reported to head office; everyone knew she reported to the Ibadan manager who mentors the new branch; the field corrected to the fact, and the first leave request a week later routes correctly because it was).

The joins made (Ch. 5, 7). User accounts linked for the 19 staff who log in; the custodian joins completed (every warehouse's custodian now an employee link — the free-text names of the Inventory era retired), the till operators joined to their session identities, the van custodian's driver's licence expiry entered into the tracking (14 months out — the worklist's first resident), and the approver map documented: who holds which two-names roles, so the separation checklist knows what to revoke. Self-service launches with the one-channel discipline — the first paper leave request is politely redirected the same day, and by week three the queue is the only channel anyone tries.

The hygiene catch (Ch. 4, 6). Month two's first status read walks the Active list against reality and finds the expected ghost: a weekend till assistant who stopped coming in the previous quarter — no resignation, no process, just absence that faded into assumption — still Active, still accruing leave, still on the roster the attendance module (module 3) is about to expect. Resolved by the document the situation deserves (the abandonment process the employment adviser confirms, the separation recorded with its trail, Left set with its date), and the lesson filed for the module ahead: the ghost was harmless in a folder-and-memory world and expensive in a system world — which is the system working, because every machine this academy has installed made the undocumented visible by refusing to pretend alongside it. The people layer ends its first quarter with 27 true records, one clean structure, a working spine, and its first ritual — the monthly status read — on the calendar with a name.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the first law
lessons.html:
The people master's scar tissue — the diseases every consultant meets in the first week of every HR engagement. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the spreadsheet workforce. Symptom: the staff list in a spreadsheet, three versions old, each department keeping its own; headcount answered differently by everyone asked. Disease: the fifth master never created (Ch. 1) — people data without a system of record. Fix: the governed load (records from documents, numbers from the series, duplicates checked), the spreadsheet retired to read-only history, and the status read instituted so the new record stays true.

Pattern 2 — the paper file as the real record. Symptom: the system holds names and dates; everything that matters lives in folders; every dispute starts with a filing-cabinet search. Disease: the master as index instead of file (Ch. 2) — attachments never made, documents never migrated. Fix: the document load (contracts, IDs, letters scanned to the record — the backlog priced once), the lifecycle documents born digital thereafter, and the folder demoted to the archive it should be.

Pattern 3 — the broken spine. Symptom: leave requests routing nowhere or to departed managers; approvals by corridor because the system's chain is wrong; an org chart nobody believes. Disease: the reports-to field unmaintained (Ch. 3) — reality and record diverged. Fix: the spine walked (every active employee, a real manager, tree-shaped), the lifecycle events re-pointing reports as they move people, and the spine's accuracy owned as part of every transfer and separation.

Pattern 4 — the ghost roster. Symptom: headcount reports nobody trusts; leave accruing for the departed; payroll (across the boundary) paying a list HR cannot vouch for. Disease: statuses changed by memory or never (Ch. 4) — the phantom-stock disease in its people form. Fix: status changes by documented events only, the monthly Active-list walk, and the separation process (module 7) as the single door to Left.

Pattern 5 — the everything-eyes HR. Symptom: any user able to list employees with personal columns; salary-adjacent fields visible to the curious; the disciplinary note that circulated. Disease: confidentiality as policy without configuration (Ch. 5) — the custody frame unenforced. Fix: the permission design (self / team / HR / sensitive tiers), the report and list-view edges audited, and module 8's permission walk on the annual calendar.

Pattern 6 — the vanity structure. Symptom: nine departments for eleven people; inflated designations; grades that map to nothing. Disease: the structure designed from aspiration instead of accountability (Ch. 3). Fix: the design hour re-run honestly — departments that are owned, titles that name roles, grades that carry real policies — and the restructure executed as the event it is.

The first law. Four tracks began with masters; the fifth begins with the most consequential one: one person, one record, whole lifecycle — the employee master is a person's record held in the firm's custody: created once from documents, governed always by events, joined everywhere by link, verified annually, and read on need, not curiosity. The structure places the person, the spine answers for them, the statuses tell the truth, and the joins make four tracks' named people real. Seven modules stand on this record; module 2 begins where every employee begins — the pipeline that found them.

recruitment.title: HR 2 — Recruitment & Onboarding
recruitment.desc: Hiring as a pipeline: the job opening born from the structure and approved as money, the applicant pool with criteria written first, structured interviews and the practical test, offers from the grade, the verification gate before day one, the onboarding checklist, and probation as a governed trial.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Hiring as a pipeline, not an event
lessons.html:
Module 1 recorded the people a firm has; this module governs how it gets them — and its thesis inverts how most trading firms actually hire: the corridor decision, the cousin's recommendation, the CV read over lunch and the offer improvised by phone. Hiring is a pipeline, not an event — a staged flow from a defined need to a confirmed colleague, with documents at every stage — and the argument for the pipeline is fourfold, worth teaching to every owner before the first requisition.

The four arguments. Signal: the corridor hire selects on impression and connection; the pipeline selects on evidence (the structured interview, the practical test — Chapter 4), and evidence beats impression at predicting who will actually run a till, keep a warehouse, or close a month — which matters because the firm is not hiring company; it is hiring capability. Fairness: candidates assessed on the same criteria, by the same process, with the record to show it — the discipline that protects the firm in dispute (the rejected candidate who alleges discrimination meets a documented process or an undocumented vibe, and only one of those defends itself) and, just as practically, protects the GOOD candidate from losing to the connected one. Repeatability: the pipeline that hired well for Ibadan hires well for Akure — the process is an asset the firm keeps, where the corridor's luck departs with whoever had it (the playbook law of every track, at the people gate). The cost frame: a bad hire costs its salary, its training, its errors, its severance, and its replacement's whole pipeline — months of cost from one skipped stage — while the pipeline's own cost is measured in days of structure; the arithmetic is not close, and the owner who has eaten one bad hire already knows it.

The funnel's stages. The module's map: the NEED defined and approved (Chapter 2 — the opening), the POOL gathered and screened (Chapter 3), the ASSESSMENT staged and scored (Chapter 4), the OFFER made from structure and accepted (Chapter 5), the VERIFICATION completed before day one (Chapter 5's second half — the stage most skipped and most expensive to skip), the ONBOARDING that converts a signature into a working colleague (Chapter 6), and the PROBATION that confirms the hire the pipeline predicted (Chapter 7). Each stage a document; each transition a decision with an owner; the whole flow readable afterwards as a record — which is what makes the pipeline improvable: source effectiveness, stage conversion, time-to-fill all become readable numbers (module 8's analytics) the corridor never produces.

The sizing honesty, up front. The eleven-person firm's pipeline is not a bureaucracy: the requisition is a one-page form the founder approves, the interviews are two structured conversations and a practical, the checklist fits on a card — the SHAPE at teaspoon scale, exactly as every track has sized its disciplines. What does not shrink with size: the criteria written before the CVs are read, the verification before joining, and the probation actually watched — the three stages where skipping is most tempting and most expensive, and the three this module guards hardest.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The job opening: the need, defined and approved
lessons.html:
The pipeline begins before any candidate exists: with the NEED, defined as a document — the job opening — and approved as the money decision it is. The requisition stage.

Born from the structure. The opening is not free text; it is assembled from module 1's architecture: the DESIGNATION (the role from the governed list — a new role means the list grows first, deliberately, not a title improvised in the advert), the GRADE (which pre-answers the offer's terms — Chapter 5's discipline starts here), the BRANCH and department (the org placement), and the REPORTING LINE (who this person will answer to — the spine extended before the person exists, so the manager who will own the hire owns the requisition too). An opening assembled this way carries its own downstream: the offer's terms, the onboarding checklist's role variant, the probation's objectives all derive from fields set at this stage — the pipeline's version of the master-data law: decisions made once at the top, inherited everywhere below.

The staffing plan frame. The opening lives against a PLAN where the firm keeps one: planned headcount per department and branch (the budget's people line — Accounts 6's budget machinery has a people twin), against which openings are raised and actual headcount reads. The plan converts hiring from reactive to governed: the opening within plan approves routinely; the opening BEYOND plan is a plan conversation (the growth that justifies it, or the workaround that avoids it) — and the read of plan-vs-actual per unit is module 8's headcount analytics born. The small-firm sizing: the 'plan' may be a one-page number per branch agreed at budget time — the shape, small.

Approval: headcount is money. The requisition's two names — the requesting manager and the approving authority (the founder, the unit head per the threshold) — because a hire is among the largest recurring financial commitments a small firm makes: the salary times twelve, times the years, plus the statutory add-ons the accountant prices — a ₦150k/month role is a multi-million-naira decision wearing a vacancy notice, and it gets the approval treatment every commitment of that size earned in every track. The approval also fixes the TERMS ENVELOPE (the grade's band — Chapter 5 will hold the offer inside it), so the negotiation later happens within a decision already made, not instead of one.

The opening as advert. Approved, the opening publishes — the role described honestly (the actual work, the actual location, the actual shift pattern: the advert that flatters the role recruits people for a job that doesn't exist, and buys the early attrition that follows), the criteria stated (Chapter 3 will insist they were written first), and the channel chosen per the role (Chapter 3's sources). The opening's lifecycle closes the stage: open while recruiting, on-hold when paused (deliberately, with a note — not drifting), closed when filled or withdrawn — the status discipline of module 1, applied to the vacancy itself, so the openings report reads true and the time-to-fill clock (module 8) has honest ends.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The applicant pool: capture & screen
lessons.html:
Candidates arrive; the pipeline's first working stage captures them as records and screens them by criteria written in advance. The pool chapter — and the discipline that makes everything after it fair and fast.

Capture: every applicant a record. Each candidate becomes a job applicant record against the opening: the CV attached, the SOURCE captured (the field that pays for itself — Chapter's end), contact details, and the status that will walk the funnel (received → screened → interviewing → offered / rejected). The capture disciplines: ALL applicants enter (the referral and the walk-in alongside the job-board stream — the parallel track where the connected candidate skips the pool is the pipeline's first corruption, and the cure is structural: one pool, one process, referrals welcome INTO it), rejection is a status with a communication (the candidate told, briefly and professionally — the employer brand argument: today's rejected applicant is tomorrow's customer, referrer, or re-applicant, and the firm that ghosts its pool is spending reputation it will want later), and the pool is retained (the strong silver-medallist from this search is the shortlist of the next one — the pool as an asset, with the personal-data custody rules of module 1 governing its retention).

Screen: criteria before CVs. The chapter's central discipline, stated as the rule it is: the screening criteria are written before the first CV is read. The reason is human and universal: criteria written after reading CVs are reverse-engineered around candidates already preferred — the impressive-but-wrong CV bends the bar toward itself, and the screen becomes a rationalisation wearing a rubric. Written first — the must-haves (the licence the role legally requires, the literacy the till demands, the availability the shift pattern needs) and the desirables (weighted, few) — the screen is a fast, fair pass: each CV against the list, in or out with a reason, the borderline batch reviewed together. Speed is a fairness feature too: the pool screened within days respects the candidates and beats competitors to the good ones — the trading firm's talent market is as real as its product market.

The screen's honesty rules. Three convictions carried from four tracks of governance: the criteria are ROLE-derived (from the opening's actual work — not a wish-list that excludes everyone who would actually take the job at the grade's band: the criteria and the terms must describe the same hire); the screen is RECORDED (in/out with reasons — thirty seconds per CV, and the record that answers the dispute or the audit); and the must-haves are MUSTS (the candidate missing a legal requirement is out regardless of charm — the pharmacist without the licence, the driver without the class — because the screen is where compliance is cheap and the tribunal is where it is not).

The source read. The captured source field, aggregated, is recruitment's supplier scorecard: which channels produce applicants, which produce HIRES, which produce hires who CONFIRM and STAY (the read that only closes when module 7's separation data joins it) — read per role type, because the channel that finds accountants rarely finds van drivers. The firm that reads its sources spends its next advert budget where hires actually came from; the one that doesn't spends it where habit points — the reading law of every track, at the recruitment gate, and module 8's analytics page carries the read.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Interviews & assessment: evidence over vibes
lessons.html:
The screened shortlist meets the firm — and this chapter is the machinery that makes those meetings produce EVIDENCE instead of impressions. The assessment stage, structured.

Rounds, defined per role. The opening's role defines its assessment path, designed once and reused (the pipeline's repeatability): the till assistant's path (screen → practical → manager conversation), the storekeeper's (screen → practical → ops interview), the accountant's (screen → technical interview → case exercise → founder conversation) — each round with a PURPOSE (what this round tests that others don't), an OWNER (who conducts and scores), and a DECISION RULE (what advances a candidate). The design discipline: rounds earn existence by adding signal — the third conversational interview that re-tests charm adds nothing the first two didn't; the practical test adds what no conversation can — and the path fits the role's stakes (two rounds for the weekend till; four for the branch manager).

Structured interviews: the same questions, scored. The evidence engine, and the chapter's core teaching: the STRUCTURED interview asks every candidate for a role the SAME core questions, anchored in the role's actual work (tell me about a time a customer disputed a price — what did you do? for the counter; walk me through how you'd receive a delivery that came short for the gate — behavioural and situational questions drawn from the very scenarios four tracks taught), scored against anchors written in advance (what a strong answer contains — the rubric that makes two interviewers comparable), with notes captured DURING (the memory that writes up interviews at day's end writes fiction by the third candidate). The argument, made once and permanently: unstructured interviews measure interview skill and interviewer mood — the confident talker beats the capable quiet one; structured interviews measure the role's evidence, and the decades of selection research the consultant can cite in one sentence say structure roughly doubles the signal. The firm hiring tills and storekeepers cannot afford to select for charm.

The practical test: the trade's truth-teller. For operational roles, the assessment this trade trusts most: the candidate DOES the work, observed and scored — the till candidate runs a mock sale, a return, and a cash-up on the training till (Accounts 3's session, as an exam); the storekeeper candidate counts a shelf, receives a mock delivery against a document, and is watched for whether they count before signing (Inventory's laws, as selection criteria); the driver candidate drives. The practical's design rules: standardised (same test, same scoring sheet), safe (training environment, no live data — the demo instance every implementation should keep exists for exactly this too), and REVEALING by construction (the test built from the role's actual failure modes — the short delivery, the disputed price — because the candidate's instinct under the standard scenario is the best single predictor the pipeline owns).

Feedback as documents; decisions on evidence. Every round's output is captured — scores, notes, recommendation — as the interview feedback record against the applicant, and the DECISION stage reads the file: scores compared, the rubric consulted, the decision minuted with its reasons (the panel that decides on the file decides differently — and defensibly — from the panel that decides on recollection and rank). The convictions that guard the stage: the highest-scoring candidate is passed over only WITH a recorded reason (the override that cannot be written down is the bias the structure exists to catch); feedback is written before interviewers confer (the senior voice that speaks first anchors every score after it); and speed remains a duty — the shortlist assessed and answered within the week, because the pipeline's fairness includes not wasting the candidates' hope.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — The offer, acceptance & the verification gate
lessons.html:
The chosen candidate gets an offer — from structure, not improvisation — and then the pipeline's most-skipped stage runs: verification, BEFORE joining. The commitment chapter.

The offer from the grade. The job offer document assembles from decisions already made: the terms from the GRADE's band (module 1's structure paying its dividend — the offer is a selection within the envelope the requisition approved, not a per-candidate negotiation that prices each hire by their bargaining nerve), the role, branch, reporting line and probation terms from the OPENING, and the conditions (subject to verification — the clause Chapter's second half enforces). The structural argument, taught to owners who like to improvise: per-candidate improvisation creates the pay-disparity time bomb (two colleagues, same role, different deals, one payday conversation away from a grievance — module 7's docket), destroys the grade structure's meaning, and negotiates from weakness (the candidate who senses improvisation negotiates; the one who meets a band selects). Flexibility lives WHERE the structure puts it: the band has a range, the range has rules (experience placing within it), and the exception beyond the band is an approval event with a name on it — the threshold law, at the offer desk.

Acceptance, captured. The offer's own lifecycle: issued (with a validity window — the open-ended offer is a liability drifting), negotiated within rules, accepted (the signed acceptance attached — the document module 1's record will be born from), or declined (with the reason captured: the decline-reason read is the offer stage's source scorecard — the band losing candidates to the market is a structure conversation, readable only if declines are recorded). Acceptance triggers the pre-joining window: the start date set, the verification gate opened, and the onboarding preparation (Chapter 6) begun — the pipeline's stages overlapping deliberately so day one arrives prepared.

The verification gate: BEFORE joining. The stage this chapter guards hardest, because its economics are brutal and its skipping is epidemic: credentials VERIFIED before the start date — the certificates confirmed with issuing institutions (the forged certificate is not rare in this market, and the practical test's existence does not excuse the paper check: the licence that lets the pharmacist practice, the qualification the role's regulator requires, are legal exposures, not formalities), references TAKEN and documented (the previous employer called — the structured three questions: role, dates, would-you-rehire — with the answers noted, because the reference that was never actually called is the pipeline's commonest quiet lie), identity confirmed against the documents module 1 will file, and — where the trade uses them — the GUARANTOR framework completed (the guarantor's own identity verified, the form signed: the cash-handling and stock-custody roles this academy has spent four tracks protecting are exactly the roles where the Nigerian trading norm of guarantors earns its paperwork). The timing law that names the chapter: verification AFTER joining is verification of a fait accompli — the failed check now means a termination (process, risk, cost) instead of a lapsed offer (a letter); the same check, two weeks earlier, is free. Verify before day one, always — the conditions clause exists so the offer survives the gate honestly, and the case study's catch (Chapter 8) is this paragraph made flesh.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Onboarding: the checklist that builds a colleague
lessons.html:
The signature is not the finish line; day one is not sit with Ngozi and watch. Onboarding is the machinery that converts an accepted offer into a working, connected, productive colleague — and like every conversion this academy has taught, it runs on a checklist with owners. The entry chapter.

Day-one readiness: prepared before arrival. The pre-joining window (Chapter 5) does the preparation, from a role-variant checklist: the employee record created from the offer's documents (module 1's governed birth), the USER account linked and permissioned (the joins of module 1 made at entry: the till operator's session identity, the storekeeper's warehouse restrictions — the permissions that took four tracks to design, granted correctly on day one instead of accreted over months), the physical kit ready (the workspace, the uniform, the device, the till float assignment), and the WELCOME real (the manager knows they are coming, the team was told, someone meets them at the door). The argument for preparation, made in the employee's voice because that is where it lands: the new hire who spends day one waiting for a login learns the firm improvises; the one whose access, kit, and schedule were ready learns the firm runs on structure — and day one's lesson is the stickiest lesson the firm will ever teach them.

The onboarding checklist, per role. The structured first weeks: the ROLE variant (the till assistant's list differs from the accountant's) covering the compliance layer (policy acknowledgments SIGNED and filed — the handbook, the code of conduct, the till and cash policies for cash-handling roles: the acknowledgment that makes module 7's disciplinary process fair, because the rule never communicated is the rule that cannot fairly be enforced), the training path ASSIGNED (module 6's machinery — the curriculum per role, with the academy's own onboarding tracks as the working example: the new consultant's twenty manuals, the new till assistant's product and till modules), the introductions scheduled (the people the role touches — the storekeeper meets the buyer whose orders they receive), and the early-days cadence (the day-one tour, the week-one check-in, the month-one review — dated, owned, done).

The buddy & the mentor. The human layer, structured lightly: a named BUDDY for the first month (the peer who answers the small questions the new hire won't ask a manager — chosen, briefed, and thanked, not assumed), distinct from the MANAGER's own cadence (the check-ins above) and from the MENTOR pattern where the firm runs one (the Ibadan manager mentoring the Akure supervisor — module 1's case study wired this into the spine; the onboarding of a branch role names it explicitly). The distinction matters because each answers different questions, and the new hire with all three lanes open asks; the one with none guesses — and guessing, at a till or a gate, is what every practical test existed to prevent.

The checklist's close. Onboarding ENDS, formally: the checklist completed and filed (every line done, dated, owned — the record that answers were they ever told? forever after), the training path's first modules passed (module 6's gates), and the handoff to probation's own machinery (Chapter 7 — onboarding builds the colleague; probation confirms the hire). The read that closes the loop: onboarding completion time and completeness per hire, and the early-attrition overlay (the hires who leave in ninety days, mapped against their onboarding records — the pattern that shows whether the firm's entries or its selections are leaking, which are different repairs). The consultant's one-line summary for owners: the first two weeks are the cheapest retention programme the firm will ever run.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Probation: the governed trial
lessons.html:
The pipeline's last stage runs after the hire starts: probation — the deliberate trial period that confirms, extends, or ends the employment — and the discipline that separates it from the date nobody watches. The confirmation chapter.

Probation as design, not default. The probation period is SET in the offer (the duration per role and grade — the common Nigerian practice of three to six months, the specifics the employment adviser confirms), and it exists for both sides: the firm confirms the pipeline's prediction against reality; the employee confirms the role against the advert (the honest advert of Chapter 2 paying off here — the role that was described truly gets confirmed into; the one that was flattered gets resigned from, at month two, with the whole pipeline's cost sunk). The period's terms are stated, not assumed: what is being assessed, what confirmation requires, what the review cadence is — because a trial whose criteria are secret is not a trial; it is a mood with a deadline.

Objectives: what confirms. The probation objectives, written at the start (the manager's duty, from the role's requirements and the onboarding's training path): the till assistant's (the training modules passed, the clean-session streak established, the mystery-count tied — the operational reads of four tracks, now serving as confirmation evidence), the storekeeper's (the receiving discipline observed, the cycle counts clean, the custody signed), the accountant's (the close participated, the reconciliations owned). The objectives law: FEW (three to five — the probation with fifteen objectives assesses nothing), OBSERVABLE (evidence the system already produces where possible — the academy's reads doing double duty again), and SHARED (the employee holds the same list the manager holds, from week one — the fairness that makes month three's decision unsurprising in either direction).

The cadence: watched, not remembered. The probation calendar, owned: the month-one check-in (onboarding's close — early problems named while they are training problems), the MID-probation review (the formal midpoint: on track, or the honest conversation that gives the employee the second half to correct — the review that makes a non-confirmation procedurally fair, because the person was told, in writing, with time to respond), and the CONFIRMATION DUE date surfaced by module 1's expiry machinery (30 days out, to the manager and HR — the lapsed probation conviction from module 1 recapped with its full weight: the probation that expires unaddressed converts to confirmation by default in most readings of practice, which is a decision made by calendar neglect instead of judgment, and the reminder is the cure).

The decision as document. Three outcomes, each a proper process: CONFIRM — the confirmation letter issued (the record's confirmation date set, the status overlay cleared — module 1's fields written by their owning event), the objectives' evidence filed with it, and the confirmation MARKED (the small ceremony the firm should not skip: the confirmed colleague told they passed, and why — the performance culture of module 5 starting on a high note); EXTEND — where genuine doubt remains and the adviser's guidance permits: the extension in writing, with the specific gaps named, the new date set, and the support offered (an extension without a plan is a deferral of a decision someone is avoiding); SEPARATE — the non-confirmation, run as the process the employment framework requires (notice per the terms, the documented trail the cadence built — the mid-review that warned, the objectives that were shared — and the exit handled with module 7's dignity disciplines, because the person who didn't fit is still a person, a reference-giver, and a voice in the market). The stage's closing read joins the pipeline's ledger: confirmation rates per source, per role, per interviewer — the number that finally grades the whole funnel, and the one module 8's analytics page waits for.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade hires for Akure
lessons.html:
The pipeline, run end to end — the Akure branch (opened in Inventory 6's case study) needs a till assistant and a storekeeper, and every chapter clocks in.

The requisitions (Ch. 2). Two openings raised from the structure: designations from the list, grade 1 and grade 2 respectively, branch Akure, reporting to the Akure supervisor — the spine extended first. Both within the branch's staffing plan (agreed at the Accounts 6 budget cycle); the founder approves in a day with the terms envelopes fixed. The adverts describe the real jobs — the Saturday shifts, the physical work, the count-before-you-sign culture — placed on one job board and the referral channel (into the pool, same process).

Pool and screen (Ch. 3). Thirty-one applicants for the till, fourteen for the store — every one a record with a source. The criteria, written before a single CV opened: the till's must-haves (numeracy check, availability for the roster, residence within reach of the branch), the store's (literacy for documents, physical capability, prior stock-handling desirable-not-required). Screens run in two sittings, reasons recorded; nine and six advance. One referral — the supervisor's neighbour — enters the pool, is screened by the same list, and does not advance: the sentence that establishes the pipeline's integrity for every hire after (she was screened like everyone; the criteria decided), delivered without drama and remembered forever.

Assessment (Ch. 4). The till path: structured interview (the disputed-price scenario, the shortpay scenario — scored against anchors) then the PRACTICAL on the training till: a mock sale, a return, a cash-up. The practical's revelation, as designed: the smoothest interviewer fumbles the cash-up arithmetic twice; a quieter candidate runs it clean, counts the drawer denominated without being told, and — the observers' note that decides it — recounts once when interrupted. The store path's practical: a shelf count and a mock short delivery against a document; two of six sign without counting (the trade's oldest failure, caught at selection for the price of a staged carton), one counts, catches the short, and annotates the document unprompted. Feedback written before conferring; decisions minuted from the file; both top scorers advanced — no overrides to record.

Offer and the gate (Ch. 5). Offers from the grades' bands — no improvisation; the till candidate negotiates within the band's rules and accepts; validity windows held. Then the verification gate earns the module its keep: the storekeeper candidate's stock-handling certificate, checked with the issuing institute, comes back unknown — the certificate is forged. The conditions clause does its quiet work: the offer lapses by letter (no termination, no drama, no risk — the check two weeks early being free, exactly as Chapter 5 priced it), the file is noted, and the runner-up — the counter who caught the short — is verified clean, offered, and accepts. The guarantor forms complete for both cash-and-custody roles; references called with the three questions, answers filed.

Onboarding and probation (Ch. 6-7). Day one arrives prepared: records born from the offer documents, users linked, the till identity and warehouse restrictions granted correctly at entry (the four tracks' permission designs, applied in an hour because the checklist knew them), kit ready, buddies named, policy acknowledgments signed — including the cash and custody policies their roles make load-bearing. Training paths assigned (the product and till modules; the receiving and counting modules — module 6's machinery previewed live). Probation objectives written and SHARED: the till's three (modules passed, clean-session streak of 30, one surprise count tied), the store's three (receiving discipline observed on five deliveries, cycle counts clean, custody count signed). Mid-reviews held on the calendar; the confirmation-due reminders fire at 30 days; and month three confirms both — the letters citing the EVIDENCE (the streak stands at 41; the five deliveries were counted before signing, every time), the small ceremony held at the branch meeting. The pipeline's ledger updates: two hires, two confirmations, one forgery caught at the gate instead of the till — and the Akure playbook (Inventory 6's branch four will take a week) gains its people chapter.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the second law
lessons.html:
The hiring layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the corridor hire. Symptom: hires appearing without openings; the connected candidate who skipped the pool; nobody able to say who approved the headcount. Disease: the event instead of the pipeline (Ch. 1-2) — selection by proximity, commitment without approval. Fix: the requisition as the only door (headcount is money and gets money's governance), one pool for all candidates including referrals, and the integrity sentence delivered early — screened like everyone; the criteria decided.

Pattern 2 — criteria after CVs. Symptom: the bar that bends toward the impressive candidate; shortlists nobody can explain against a list. Disease: the rationalisation wearing a rubric (Ch. 3). Fix: criteria written and filed before the pool opens, the screen recorded in/out with reasons, and the must-haves held as musts — especially the legal ones.

Pattern 3 — the charm selection. Symptom: hires who interviewed brilliantly and work badly; the confident talker beating the capable quiet one, repeatedly. Disease: unstructured interviews measuring interview skill (Ch. 4). Fix: the structured core questions with scoring anchors, feedback written before conferring, and the practical test for every operational role — the trade's truth-teller, built from its actual failure modes.

Pattern 4 — verification after joining, or never. Symptom: the forged certificate discovered at month four; the reference never actually called; the guarantor form blank in the file of the till operator with a drawer variance. Disease: the gate skipped (Ch. 5) — the check that was free two weeks early now priced as a termination. Fix: the conditions clause in every offer, the verification checklist owned in the pre-joining window, and the rule absolute: no start date before the gate clears.

Pattern 5 — 'sit with Ngozi'. Symptom: new hires learning by osmosis; access accreted over months; policies never acknowledged and therefore never fairly enforceable; early attrition nobody maps. Disease: onboarding as improvisation (Ch. 6). Fix: the role-variant checklist, day-one readiness prepared in the pre-joining window, acknowledgments signed and filed, and the early-attrition overlay read against onboarding records.

Pattern 6 — the unwatched probation. Symptom: confirmations by calendar lapse; non-performers confirmed by neglect and separated expensively later; probationers who never knew what confirmed. Disease: the trial as a mood with a deadline (Ch. 7). Fix: objectives few, observable, and shared; the mid-review on the calendar; the expiry reminder wired; and the decision — confirm, extend, separate — always a document with evidence.

The second law. The first law made the person's record; the second governs how people enter it: hiring is a pipeline, not an event — the need defined and approved before advertising, one pool screened by criteria written first, assessment on evidence with the practical as the trade's truth-teller, offers from structure, credentials verified before day one, and the first ninety days managed as deliberately as the first interview. Each stage a document, each transition owned, the whole funnel readable — and the pipeline's product is not a signature but a confirmed colleague whose file already tells their story. Module 3 begins the working rhythm that story now joins: attendance, shifts, and the roster that keeps a branch trading.
